[GReeeeN] Why should I use a card with no international fees if I’m being charged in AUD?
[trixieb] NordVPN and other VPN companies via TopCashback AU that I have posted seem to trade in USD. Some of them including NordVPN seem to auto-convert to AUD (estimate) on the website when we access from Australia. The financial institutions may view the order as an international transaction so it's best to pay with a card without international transaction fees.
Please see this OzBargain reference: Australian Sites that can incur a fee for transactions
Regardless of the card used, if using PayPal AU, there could be a currency conversion fee from PayPal AU. I had paid this extra PayPal currency conversion fee with NordVPN and PureVPN although I had used a credit card without international transaction fees. If you have a USD balance in your PayPal AU account (using Wise), there may not be an extra charge. I'm not familiar with this as I don't have Wise.
There is another currency conversion fee that we have no control of and is written in my tips and TopCashback AU terms. NordVPN and other VPN companies seem to report the price charged in USD to TopCashback AU which is converted to AUD in our TopCashback accounts. The currency conversion fee is relative to the price paid and is ineligible for cashback. Hence the reported amount paid in TopCashback AU is usually less than what we actually paid. Cashback is 100% of this reported amount (after deducting the fee) and not what we actually paid.
For the basic 2-year (+ 3 extra months) plan, this offer may cost a minimum of around $6 (after 100% cashback less TCB AU fees) if using a card without international transaction fees.
